---
title: "9 · Reservoir Computing"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

Reservoir computing forecasts without training the network. Training every weight of a recurrent network through the history is slow and costly, and Koopman theory suggests another route, lifting the dynamics into many observables where it becomes nearly linear. A fixed random driven system, the echo state network, provides such a lift, and only a linear readout is fitted by one ridge solve. We define the echo state property and fading memory, measure the memory capacity, and compare the reservoir with trained networks on the benchmark signals. Run in a closed loop on the Lorenz system, the reservoir follows the weather for a few Lyapunov times and reproduces the climate. The same idea works with other systems. An elementary cellular automaton combines the bits of the input by logic, and a register of interacting qubits forgets its start only when its dynamics is chaotic, which the level-spacing ratio of its spectrum reveals.
